All other checks green. tsc, eslint, vitest (1002 tests / 6 skipped) all pass. npm run fitness:db not runnable (no DATABASE_URL in this env); T-0087 fitness:db failures are all DATABASE_URL errors — pre-existing db failures (ADV-4, grant-editor 30-vs-29 count, dual-control 031) confirmed pre-T-0087 by git diff.

role_criticality_fail_analysis.mechanism: role-criticality-isolation.sh (T-0040) greps all files changed vs merge-base with dev. FROZEN_PATHS_RE includes 'migrations/.*\.sql'. T-0087's migrations/044_tier.sql lands in the diff and triggers FF-RC5/FF-RC6. The check has an established MIGRATION_EXCLUDE_RE exclusion list for sibling migrations; it currently lists 030/031/043 (T-0030/T-0044/T-0024) with attribution comments. The check's own comment explains: 'The exclusion list must only name migrations owned by other known tasks; any new T-0040 migration would still be caught.' The precedent is strict: each migration PR that trips this check is REQUIRED to add its entry to MIGRATION_EXCLUDE_RE with an ownership comment (git log: 7786cc9 for 043, edaab9e for 031).
role_criticality_fail_analysis.what_is_wrong_with_coder_claim: The coder wrote 'green post-merge to dev'. This framing is false: the check does NOT auto-green on merge. The correct fix is adding '044_tier' to MIGRATION_EXCLUDE_RE with an attribution comment, exactly as T-0030/T-0044/T-0024 did. 'Will be green post-merge' is a D-056 violation — the branch must be equivalent to dev, i.e., the fix must be applied on the branch before merge.
role_criticality_fail_analysis.required_fix: In ci/checks/role-criticality-isolation.sh, extend MIGRATION_EXCLUDE_RE to include 044_tier: MIGRATION_EXCLUDE_RE='^migrations/(030_grant_proposed_confirmed|031_grant_confirmed2_by|043_invoke_proposal|044_tier)\.sql$' and add a comment block attributing 044_tier.sql to T-0087 (E12.6 tier column on config+data tables). This is a one-line change mirroring the 030/031/043 precedent.

findings.issue: MIGRATION_EXCLUDE_RE does not include 044_tier.sql, causing role-criticality-isolation.sh to fail with FF-RC5/FF-RC6. This is a required update per established precedent: every sibling migration (030, 031, 043) was added to this list by its owning PR. The branch must be green before merge (D-056); 'post-merge green' is not acceptable.
findings.suggestion: Add 044_tier to MIGRATION_EXCLUDE_RE: '^migrations/(030_grant_proposed_confirmed|031_grant_confirmed2_by|043_invoke_proposal|044_tier)\.sql$' and add an attribution comment block explaining that 044_tier.sql is owned by T-0087 E12.6. One-line change. See commits 7786cc9 (043) and edaab9e (031) as the exact template.

findings.issue: decidePromote is called with hardcoded currentTier: 'draft' instead of the actual artifact tier. This makes the NOT_IN_DRAFT code path in decidePromote permanently dead from the endpoint. The ADR §4.3 specifies decidePromote validates 'both the source state and the human-gate signal'; the endpoint bypasses the source-state check entirely. The 409 NOT_IN_DRAFT response still fires (via promoteTier line 195), so correctness is preserved — but the usage violates the contract of decidePromote and makes the code misleading. Any caller reading the handler assumes decidePromote checked the tier; it did not.
findings.suggestion: Either: (a) call decidePromote after the FOR UPDATE SELECT (passing the real currentTier from rowRes.rows[0].tier), replacing both the decidePromote call and the manual `if (currentTier !== 'draft')` check inside promoteTier with a single decidePromote call; or (b) rename the pre-DB call to checkAgentGate (extract only the agent-type check) to honestly represent what is being tested. Option (a) is the correct ADR §4.3 alignment.

findings.issue: FF-1 iterates tier_bearing_tables.txt line by line but the grep is applied over ALL_SQL_STRIPPED without anchoring to the specific table name. The check passes if ANY migration contains `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS tier text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'`, not specifically the one for the table being checked. This means if, say, only application gets the column, the check would still pass for registry_def, grant, and record. Weak for a registry-based anti-drift guard.
findings.suggestion: Anchor the per-table grep: grep for '${table}' AND the tier column pattern in the same expression, e.g. grep -iqE "ALTER TABLE choros\.\"?${table}\"?.*ADD COLUMN.*tier|ALTER TABLE.*${table}.*tier". This matches the `known_tenant_tables.txt` pattern from T-0115 more faithfully. Low urgency (migration is correct; this is a check quality nit), but worth hardening before E12 adds more tables to the registry.

findings.issue: DEV_TENANT_ID from process.env is used directly in the withTenantTx call (line 317) without a pre-call UUID validation. assertUuidShape is called inside withTenantTx (line 81), so injection is blocked, but if DEV_TENANT_ID is not a valid UUID the error message is a generic '400 VALIDATION tenantId must be a valid UUID' with no hint that it came from an env var. Low-risk because the default is hardcoded and env vars are operator-controlled.
findings.suggestion: Add a startup-time assertion: if DEV_TENANT_ID does not match UUID_RE, throw or log a clear error at module load. Not blocking — the UUID check inside withTenantTx is the safety net.
